classification.difficultyReason: Combines tangent–radius perpendicularity, equal radii, central and reflex angles, and the alternate segment theorem.

content.prompt: Find the values of the pronumerals.

spec.description: Schematic circle with horizontal tangent PQ at the bottom vertex, an inscribed triangle, two dashed radii and an unlabelled centre dot. Preserve the minor and reflex central sectors and the full tangent-to-chord 150° sector, which includes the bottom radius. Source proportions are schematic rather than angle measurements.
spec.mathematics: x and y are the base angles of the triangle formed by two radii and their chord. z is its minor central angle; w is the reflex central angle. v is the angle at a circumference point on the minor arc between the chord endpoints.
spec.answerVisibility: Only the given 150° and unknown labels x, y, z, w and v appear in the question diagram.

answer.worked:
The radius is perpendicular to the tangent.
$$\begin{align*}x&=150^\circ-90^\circ\\x&=60^\circ\end{align*}$$
The two radii are equal, so the base angles are equal.
$$y=60^\circ$$
Angles in a triangle sum to $180^\circ$.
$$\begin{align*}z&=180^\circ-60^\circ-60^\circ\\z&=60^\circ\end{align*}$$
Angles around a point sum to $360^\circ$.
$$\begin{align*}w&=360^\circ-60^\circ\\w&=300^\circ\end{align*}$$
$$v=150^\circ$$
Alternate segment theorem.
